title: Substitutionary Atonement
definition: Substitutionary Atonement is Christ's work of standing in the place of sinners, bearing their guilt, and dying for their sins.
summary: Substitutionary Atonement teaches that Christ made atonement by bearing the guilt and judgment of sinners in their place.
christFocus: Jesus Christ is the Lamb of God who bears sin and gives His life for His people.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
This doctrine focuses on the saving meaning of Christ's death: He stands where sinners should have stood and bears what they deserved. It is not merely an example of love or courage, though it is both; it is the atoning sacrifice that reconciles guilty people to God. Substitutionary atonement explains how mercy can be given without justice being denied.

Scripture teaches that sin brings guilt, judgment, and separation from God. At the cross, Jesus does not simply sympathize with sinners from a distance; He takes the sinner's place as the obedient Son, the spotless Lamb, and the willing sacrifice.

This doctrine connects the whole Gospel together. Forgiveness, justification, reconciliation, peace, and assurance are possible because Christ bore sin in the place of His people and rose again as the accepted Savior.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Without substitution the cross loses its saving center. Sinners need more than inspiration; they need guilt removed, wrath satisfied, and peace made. This doctrine keeps the Gospel clear when culture wants a cross without judgment or a Savior without sacrifice.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Come to the cross as one who needed a Substitute, not merely a teacher. Worship Christ for standing in your place. When preaching or teaching, make clear that Jesus did not simply suffer with sinners—He suffered for sinners.
